simple.meaning: יְלָלָה (yᵉlâlâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a howling.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יְלָלָה (H3215) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 15:8, with occurrences in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Zephaniah, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְלָלָה (H3215) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יְלָלָה (H3215) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יְלָלָה (yᵉlâlâh) / H3215 is traced through Isaiah 15:8, Jeremiah 25:36, Zephaniah 1:10, Zechariah 11:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3215. yelalah יְלָלָה noun feminine howling ; — וִילָלָה Zeph 1:10 ; construct יִָֽלֲלַת Jer 25:36 ; Zech 11:3 ; יִלְלָתָהּ Isa 15:8 (twice in verse); — howling in distress 15:8 (twice in verse) (|| זְעָקָה ), Jer 25:36 (of leaders of flock, metaphor for princes; || צעקה קול ), Zeph 1:10 (|| id. ); הָרֹעִים יִָֽלֲלַת קול Zech 11:3 ( רעים metaphor for princes).
